_why:
Sixty-one edges joining the DIRDs to their authors, the institutions those authors worked for, and the research domains the papers sit in. Every one already carried a precise note; none carried a source.

Each now cites what its own note rests on. Where the note turns on authorship or affiliation it takes the DIA's 9 January 2018 list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which is what credits each paper to a named author and institution - 39 of the 61 say so explicitly. Every edge also takes the released document itself, by the URLs recorded in research/_dird-verification.json, which is the file produced by downloading all 32 PDFs and reading their covers rather than by trusting a filename.

The list is cited at fas.org/publication/aatip-list/ rather than irp.fas.org/dia/aatip-list.pdf, because the latter returns HTTP 202 with an empty body and its Wayback capture recorded the same.

Tiers are left exactly as the notes set them. Several are deliberately Tier 2 and say why - the Teofilo edge because the cover author field is redacted under (b)(6) and reads 'Authors' plural, so co-authorship cannot be excluded. Attaching a source does not upgrade a claim, and nothing here was re-tiered.
